SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

Date October 20, 19 38.

Subject Shanghai Wharf Coolies Life Improvement Society - pamphlets in
support of, found in Jessfield Area, O.O.L.

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by A. Logan (1)

Copies of a pamphlet entitled "An Urgent Manifesto issued
by the whole body of the Shanghai Municipality Wharf Coolies"
advocating wharf coolies to render support to the "Shanghai
Wharf Coolies Life Improvement Society (上海市碼頭工人生話改進社.)
were found pasted on electric poles in the Jessfield area on
October 18, 1938. A full translation of the pamphlet (a copy
is attached herewith) reads as follows:-

"AN URGENT MANIFESTO ISSUED BY THE WHOLE BODY OF THE
SHANGHAI MUNICIPALITY WHARF COOLIES

"We, Tsai Yoong Sung (蔡荣生), etc., participated
in the 'Shanghai Wharf Coolies Life Improvement Society'
under the leadership of Kying Sze Chuen (景仕權) with
a view to struggling for the betterment of the treatment
of the wharf coolies. This Society has been registered
with the Central and Local Kuomintang.

"When the Sino-Japanese hostilities broke out last
year, we all went to work with the armies in the front
to fulfil our duty towards the country with the result
that the Society became temporarily inactive.

"Tsau Tsung Chu (朱春駒), Hsia Vung Yoong (夏文荣),
and Wu Dah Tsung (吳大振), availing themselves upon
this opportunity formed an illegal body called the 'Wharf
Coolies Association (碼頭工人協會).' They are at present
planning to overthrow this Society by first causing dis-
sension among its members.

"All the wharf coolies are urged to support the 'Life
Improvement Society' and not to recognize the 'Wharf Coolies
Association.'"

事由 上海码头工人生活改进社——在越界筑路区（O.O.L.）极司菲尔（Jessfield）地区发现支持该社的传单。

由特务督察廖仲坚（Liao Chung Chien）撰写，经 A. Logan (1) 转呈

1938年10月18日，在极司菲尔（Jessfield）地区的电线杆上发现了张贴的题为《上海全市码头工人全体紧急宣言》的传单副本，该宣言呼吁码头工人支持“上海码头工人生活改进社”。传单的完整译文如下（附副本一份）：-

“上海全市码头工人全体紧急宣言

“我们，蔡荣生等人，在景仕權的领导下参加了‘上海码头工人生活改进社’，旨在为改善码头工人的待遇而斗争。本会已向国民党中央及地方党部注册。

“去年中日战事爆发时，我们均前往前线随军服务，以尽报国之责，致使本会暂时停止活动。

“朱春駒、夏文荣和吳大振利用此机会，组建了一个名为‘码头工人协会’的非法团体。他们目前正计划首先在本会成员中制造分歧，从而推翻本会。

“特此呼吁所有码头工人支持‘生活改进社’，不承认‘码头工人协会’。”

    "The superior organ has been requested to investigate
the dispute while the wharf coolies are hereby appraised
by this manifesto of what had actually taken place."
    It will be recalled that the "Shanghai Wharf Coolies Life
Improvement Society" was formed on 28/5/36 by a number of persons
headed by one Kying Sze Chuen (景仕權) with the object of first
gaining influence over wharf coolies and then extorting money
from wharf authorities by demanding from the latter payment of
fees for every package of commodities loaded and unloaded at
the wharfs. Its main office at No.736 Chung Kung Road (Military
Road), O.O.L., was raided and suppressed by the Chinese Police
on April 10, 1937, while its branch in the Settlement at 10/625
Yunnan Road was closed by the Municipal Police on February 19,
1937, as their existence was deemed by the authorities to be
undesirable. Since then the members of the Society have not
been heard of.
    The recent appearance of pamphlets in the Jessfield area
shows that the members of the Society possibly taking advantage
of the absence of a wharf coolies' union here since the outbreak
of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1937, intend to revive its
activities.
    The information contained in the pamphlet that a "Wharf
Coolies Association" has been organized cannot be verified nor
can the identity of any of the persons mentioned therein be
ascertained.
    Detectives have been instructed to keep this matter in view
and anything of interest will form the subject of a further report.

    “已请求上级机关调查此纠纷，同时通过本宣言告知码头工人实际发生的情况。”
    回顾可知，“上海码头工人生活改进社”于1936年5月28日由景仕權为首的一群人成立，其目的是先取得对码头工人的影响力，然后通过要求码头当局支付每包装卸货物的费用来勒索钱财。其位于越界筑路区（O.O.L.）军工路（Chung Kung Road）736号的总办事处于1937年4月10日被华警搜查并取缔，而其位于租界内云南路625号10室的分支机关于1937年2月19日被工部局警务处关闭，因为当局认为其存在令人不快。此后，未再听到该社成员的消息。
    近期在极司菲尔（Jessfield）地区出现传单，表明该社成员可能利用自1937年中日战事爆发以来此地缺乏码头工人工会的机会，意图恢复活动。
    传单中称已组织“码头工人协会”的信息无法核实，其中提到的任何人的身份也无法查明。
    已指示侦探留意此事，任何有趣的情况将成为进一步报告的主题。

Section 1, Special Branch.
REPORT
File No. 7523
Date October 25, 37.
19

Subject Shanghai Wharf Coolies Life Improvement Society - activities.

Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by C. Sanford a J.

On October 20, 1937, a notice signed by one Mr. Kying
Sze-chuen , chairman of the Shanghai Wharf Coolies Life Improve-
ment Society, now defunct, was inserted in the advertisement
columns of the Sin Wan Pao warning all wharf coolies who are
members of the above mentioned Society to guard against being
utilized or employed by the "enemy" for the transportation of
ammunition and goods or in any other capacity. The notice gave
no address or any other particulars which would show the origin
of the notice.

Inquiries made at the offices of the Sin Wan Pao learned
that on October 19, a male Chinese called at the above offices
and requested the staff to publish the above notice. The charge
for publishing the notice was duly paid and the person who ten-
dered it left without giving his name or address.

As will be seen from the attached reports, the Shanghai
Wharf Coolies Life Improvement came into existence on May 28,
1936 and application by the Society to register with the local
Kuomintang was refused by the said Authorities. Its offices
at 736/8 Chung Koong Road, O.O.I. were raided and closed down
by the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau on April 10, 1937
and since that time nothing has been heard of it.

It would appear that the executive members of the above
mentioned Society taking advantage of the present disturbed
times evidently intend to revive their activities to gain
control over the local wharf coolies.

It is further learned that the local Kuomintang Head-
quarters has issued instructions to the Press Censorship Office
to prohibit the publication in local newspapers of all news or
notices issued by the above Society.

D.C. (Special Branch). Noted

日期 1937年10月25日。

事由 上海码头工人生活改进社——活动情况。

由特务督察施思坚（Shih Ssu-chien）撰写，经 C. Sanford a J. 转呈

1937年10月20日，现已解散的上海码头工人生活改进社主席景仕權先生签署的一份通告刊登在《新闻报》的广告栏中，警告上述社团的所有码头工人成员，警惕被“敌人”利用或雇佣来运输弹药和货物，或从事其他任何工作。该通告未提供地址或任何其他能显示通告来源的细节。

向《新闻报》报社查询后获悉，10月19日，一名中国男子来到上述报社，要求工作人员刊登上述通告。刊登通告的费用已如数支付，递交通告者未留下姓名或地址便离开了。

从附件报告可以看出，上海码头工人生活改进社成立于1936年5月28日，该社向国民党地方党部注册的申请被有关当局拒绝。其位于越界筑路区（O.O.I.）军工路736/8号的办事处于1937年4月10日被上海市政府警察局搜查并关闭，此后未再听到有关该社的消息。

看来，上述社团的执行委员们显然打算利用目前的动荡局势，恢复活动以控制当地码头工人。

另悉，国民党地方党部已向新闻检查处发出指令，禁止在当地报纸上发表上述社团发布的所有新闻或通告。

October 20, 1937.
Afternoon Translation.

To Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

PRECAUTIONS AGAINST WORKERS BEING UTILIZED BY THE ENEMY :
WHARF COOLIES' LIFE IMPROVEMENT SOCIETY ISSUES NOTICE

On October 19, the Wharf Coolies' Life
Improvement Society issued the following circular notice
addressed to all wharf coolies :-
"The country is face to face with a grave crisis.
It is a matter of grief that some wharf coolies are being
utilized by the enemy. Mr. Yih Hsia-sung (葉夏聲),
Chairman of the Society, has asked the higher authorities
for permission to reorganize this Society. A notice has
been received from the authorities stating that the matter
has been referred to the local Tangpu to be dealt with.
"At the present time when the nation is engaged
in a war of defence, the people should support the Government
so as to strengthen the resistance to the enemy. This
Society hereby warns all wharf coolies who are registered
with this body not to allow themselves, at any time, to
be utilized by the enemy, to unload or remove war materials
or goods or to undertake any other work on behalf of the
enemy. The pretext that they had been compelled to work
for the enemy will not be accepted.
"This Society will deal most severely with
any coolie committing the above offences. The Society
will request the authorities to give compassionate grants
to a coolie who has been injured because he had refused to
work for the enemy".

下午译文。

致《公报》及其他当地报纸：-

防范工人被敌人利用：码头工人生活改进社发布通告

10月19日，码头工人生活改进社向所有码头工人发布了以下通函通知：-
“国家面临严重危机。令人悲痛的是，一些码头工人正被敌人利用。本社主席葉夏聲先生已请求上级当局批准重组本社。已收到当局通知，称此事已移交地方党部处理。
“在当前国家进行防御战争之际，民众应支持政府，以加强抗敌力量。本社特此警告所有在本社注册的码头工人，在任何时候不得允许自己被敌人利用，卸载或搬运战争物资或货物，或代表敌人从事任何其他工作。以被迫为敌人工作为借口将不被接受。
“本社将对犯有上述罪行的任何苦力予以最严厉的处置。本社将请求当局向因拒绝为敌人工作而受伤的苦力提供抚恤金。”

SIN WAN PAO - P.M. 20-10-37
WHARF WORKERS WARNED NOT TO WORK FOR ENEMY

The following notice published by the Shanghai
Municipality Wharf Coolies' Livelihood Improvement
Association appears in the advertisement columns of the
"Shun Pao" and other local newspapers to-day :-

"Owing to lack of organization among local
wharf coolies, it is regrettable that a number of them are
working for the enemy. The request made by Mr. Yih Auh-
sing (葉夏聲), Chairman of the Board of Directors of
this Association, for a re-organization has been approved
by the highest authorities who have directed the local
Tangpu to handle the matter.

"In view of the national crisis, all wharf
hands should work in unison for the support of the
Government. Apart from drawing up concrete measures
for the relief of unemployed wharf workers, this Association
hereby warns all workers who have registered themselves
with this Association to refrain from being utilized or
employed by the enemy for the transportation of munitions
and goods or in any other capacity. The pretext that
they had been compelled to do so will not be entertained.
Should such a case come to the knowledge of this Association,
the offender will be severely dealt with. This Association,
however, will request the authorities to grant compensation
to workers who have been injured or otherwise ill-treated
for refusing to work for the enemy."

《新闻报》 - 1937年10月20日下午
警告码头工人勿为敌人工作

今日，《申报》及其他当地报纸的广告栏刊登了上海特别市码头工人生活改进协会发布的以下通告：-

“由于本地码头工人缺乏组织，令人遗憾的是，其中一些人正在为敌人工作。本协会理事会主席葉夏聲先生提出的重组请求已获最高当局批准，当局已指示地方党部处理此事。

“鉴于国家危机，所有码头工人应团结一致支持政府。除了制定具体措施救济失业码头工人外，本协会特此警告所有在本协会注册的工人， refrain from being utilized or employed by the enemy for the transportation of munitions and goods or in any other capacity（避免被敌人利用或雇佣来运输军火和货物，或从事其他任何工作）。以被迫这样做为借口将不予考虑。若本协会得知此类案件，违规者将受到严厉处置。然而，本协会将请求当局向因拒绝为敌人工作而受伤或遭受其他虐待的工人给予赔偿。”

Subject Shanghai Wharf Coolies Life Improvement Society - further report.

Made by....D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien    Forwarded by....J. Boyne D.S.I

With reference to the attached letter from the Shanghai
City Government Police Bureau regarding the above subject:
discreet and careful enquiries have been pursued at various
wharves in Shanghai, but no evidence has been obtained to show
that there has been any renewal of activity by the Shanghai
Wharf Coolies Life Improvement Society, since its offices at
736/8 Chung Koong Road, O.O.L. were raided and closed down by
the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau on April 10, 1937.
At the end of February, 1937 several responsible members
of this Society established an office in the Jing Ji Cotton Hong
at No.12, Lane 286 Canton Road, but this office was subsequently
closed down because of lack of financial support.
The Society's former offices at No.10, Lane 265 Yunnan
Road, which was closed down by Municipal Police on February 19,
1937 was periodically visited by detectives, but no signs of
renewed activity were observed.
Detectives have been instructed to keep this matter in
view, and anything of interest will form the subject of another
report.

D.C.(Special Branch).                                D.S.I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE.

Translation of Letter from Shanghai City Government Police Bureau.

CONFIDENTIAL "致" No.42                                April      19,    1937.

S.M.P. Headquarters,
Shanghai.

Sirs,

In reply to your letter of March 27, enclosing a copy
of a Police Report on the subject of the Shanghai Wharf coolies
Livelihood Improvement Association at No.736 Chun Koong Road
and a copy of its regulations, I have to inform you that our
Ying Ziang Kong Branch Bureau was instructed to have the
institution suppressed immediately. Later a report was
received from the Branch Bureau to the following effect:-

"In accordance with your instructions enquiries were
instituted by Inspector Yao Vung Yin, attached to the Chun
Koong Road Sub Station and it was ascertained that some
members of the staff secured their positions in the institution
by putting up cash securities and that the Chairman, Kyung
Sze Chuen (景仕程), was in Nanking and the officer in charge,
Yang Nai Yue (杨乃岳), could not be located. It has a committee
for the control of the cash securities established on premises
No.10, Lane 265, Wei Ioh Li alleyway off Yunnan Road. The men
sent out by the institution to carry out its activities appear
to be engaged in fraudulent practices. The furniture of the
institution has been sealed up and the landlord of the premises
ordered to sign a bond not to lease his premises again to those
for the formation of illegal organisations. Huang Shou Shek
and others, members of the Association, having made statements
expressing their repentance have returned to their native places,
but Chi Yuin Chien, Zing Paung Yen, Taung Li Zung and Yoh Yong
Kong, who were reluctant to furnish bonds and instigated others
to ignore our order, have been expelled from our district.
It has also been learned that the officer in charge is now
carrying on his activities in the so-called "Jing Ji Cotton
Hong" (進基紗花申莊), at No.12 Koong Zung Li (公順里) off Canton
Road"

As No.12 Koong Zung Li, Canton Road, is situated within
your jurisdiction, I have to inform you as above and hope you
will take such suppressive measures against them as you may
deem proper.

Tsai Chin Chun
Chief of the S.C.G.P.B.

movement among wharf labourers become popular. They plan first

Jukong Wharf, and Point Island, and then demand that the wharf
authorities to pay the Society one cent per every package of
merchandise loaded or unloaded. This income would be considerable
and it is estimated that, apart from defraying the expenses of the
society, the promoters would be able to enrich themselves with

The Shanghai Municipality Wharf Coolies Life
Improvement Society (上海市碼頭工人生存改進社) came
into existence on May 28, 1936 with a head office at No.736
Military Road, Yangtszepoo, O.O.L., and a branch office at
No.29 Sze Ming Li, Avenue Dubail. The alleged object of this society
is to promote mutual friendship among wharf coolies and to
improve their livelihood. It is now being managed by the
following committee members :-
Executive Committee :
Tso Kying-ding (卓敬亭)
Zao Bei-zoen (趙勃生)
Wu Yuin-ching (胡雲卿)
Wong Yoong-nien (王永年)
Kying Sze-chuen (景仕權)

Li Pah-liang (李伯良)
Liu Yoh-zai (劉育才)
Yue Siao-pan (葉小潘)

In the forenoon of September 8, a dispute took place
between Kying Sze-chuen (景仕權), a member of the Executive
Committee and two Chinese named Zien Siu-tsing (錢秀清)
and Loh Tsai-fah (陸才發) over the question of employment.
According to Zien Siu-tsing and Loh Tsai-fah, Kying Sze-chuen
had promised to employ them in the capacity of foremen at a
monthly salary of $60, provided that they subscribed $150.00
each towards the expenses of forming the society. Kying Sze-
chuen, however, denied that he had promised to employ Zien
and Loh as foremen, and that they were two of the seventeen
promoters.

made to the local Tangpu and the Bureau of Social Affairs
for registration, no permission for the inauguration of
the society had been obtained.

who are wharf coolies in Chinese controlled territory and
French Concession. These coolies are required to pay $0.50

have been collected. In order to cover the expenses of the
society, the promoters have subscribed some $5,000.00. The
monthly expenditure is approximately $160.00 and a total of
$6,700.00 has been spent since the formation of the society.
    It is worthy of note to state that Kying Sze-chuen
was sentenced in 1927 to 8 months' imprisonment on a charge
of demanding money by threats and in 1933 to one year's
imprisonment on a charge of attempted extortion.

Shanghai Municipality Wharf Coolies Livelihood Improvement
